Package index

Parameter estimation

Maximum likelihood estimation of the parameters of the four neutral models. The logl values of optim_ewens(), optim_pitman() and optim_etienne() are on the same scale, so nested models can be compared directly.

optim_ewens()
Maximum likelihood estimation of \(\theta\) based on Ewens sampling formula
optim_pitman()
Maximum likelihood estimation of \(\theta\) and \(\sigma\) based on Pitman sampling formula
optim_etienne()
Maximum likelihood estimation of \(\theta\) and \(m\) based on Etienne sampling formula
optim_multideme()
Maximum likelihood estimation of local immigration rates \((m_1,...,m_K)\) based on the K-deme sampling formula

Etienne sampling formula

Likelihood of Etienne’s sampling formula and its coefficients.

logl_etienne()
Log-likelihood of Etienne's sampling formula
logkda()
Etienne's coefficients \(K(D,A)\) of the sampling formula with dispersal limitation

Generation of species abundance distributions

Exact simulation of the Ewens and Pitman models.

generate_hoppe_urn()
Generation of a neutral partition given parameter \(\theta\) using the Griffiths-Engen-McCloskey representation
generate_hoppe_urn0()
Generation of a neutral partition given parameter \(\theta\) using Hoppe's urn
generate_pitman_urn()
Generation of a Pitman partition given parameters \(\theta\) and \(\sigma\) from the Griffiths-Engen-McCloskey representation

Number of species

Expected number of species, overall or above an abundance threshold.

kest()
Expected number of classes given parameter \(\theta\) and sample size J for the Hoppe urn model
kest_gt()
Expected number of classes with more than N individuals given parameters \(\theta\) and sample size J using the species frequency spectrum
kest_gt0()
Expected number of classes with more than N individuals given parameters \(\theta\) and sample size J using the GEM representation
